Common billing myths — and what’s real

Myth: Therapy is only for crisis.
Many people assume therapy is only for extreme situations.

Truth: Therapy is useful for navigation, skills-building, and steady support as much as for acute crises. Investing earlier often reduces needed intensity later.

Myth: Sliding scale means lower quality.
Sliding scale simply adjusts access, not care standards.

Truth: Adjusted fees reflect an effort to broaden access. Clinical standards and confidentiality remain the same for all clients.

Foundational commitments (how I work)

Safety

An emotionally contained space with clear consent, boundaries, and confidentiality.

Collaboration

We set goals together and revisit progress; you guide priorities.

Brief case notes — anonymized examples

Client A — Managing burnout

Eight focused sessions to restructure work-life boundaries and reframed expectations; practical tools reduced evening rumination.

Client B — Relationship patterns

A series of sessions looked at attachment patterns and communication skills; couple-level referrals provided when appropriate.

Fee-related questions

Do you offer a sliding scale? Occasionally and based on availability and need — we will discuss openly during an initial contact.

Can I use insurance? I provide superbills for out-of-network reimbursement; I do not bill insurance directly.

What about cancellations? A 48-hour notice is appreciated. Late cancellations or no-shows may be charged up to the full session fee.

Ready to plan next steps?

If these options resonate, choose a time for an initial consultation. We’ll clarify fit, goals, and scheduling.

Questions people often bring up

Concise, practical answers to help orient you before we talk.
How do I know if therapy is a good fit?
Therapy often feels useful when you notice patterns that cause recurring distress, or when a life change feels harder to manage alone. The first few sessions are about assessing fit, goals, and practical steps. There is no obligation to continue beyond an initial meeting.
How do confidentiality and records work?
Your sessions are confidential. Notes are kept securely and in alignment with professional ethics. Exceptions exist where safety is at risk (harm to self or others) or as required by law; these limits are discussed during intake.
What therapeutic modalities do you use?
I draw from {{MODALITIES}} and integrate evidence-informed approaches tailored to your needs. Our work is collaborative and adapted over time.
Can I switch to telehealth or in-person?
Yes. Telehealth is available across {{STATE}} except where restricted by licensure. In-person sessions are offered in {{CITY}} when scheduled. We will confirm logistics on booking.
What should I prepare for my first session?
Think about what brings you now, your immediate goals, and any recent stressors. I will ask brief administrative and clinical questions to form a shared plan. No prior preparation is required.

Clarifying a few persistent myths

Therapy = weakness?
Actually, seeking help is an active, courageous step toward skill-building and well-being.
One-size-fits-all?
Treatment is tailored. We co-create goals and methods that fit your life and values.
Immediate cures?
Therapy is a process. Progress is measurable but rarely instantaneous.

Small case snapshots

Young professional facing anxiety
Structured sessions provided cognitive tools and behavioral experiments. After several months, the client reported improved sleep and calmer decision-making.
Midlife transition and meaning
Exploratory work focused on values, boundaries, and practical planning for career adjustment; progress combined reflective work and actionable steps.

Practical policies

Cancellation and payment
Please give 48 hours' notice for cancellations when possible. Payment is due at the time of service; I can provide receipts for reimbursement. Discuss exceptions directly.
Crisis procedures
I do not provide emergency services. If you are at immediate risk, call emergency services or local crisis lines. We will create a safety plan in-session if needed.
Schedule an introductory meeting

If you have other concerns that aren’t listed, feel free to email {{EMAIL}} or call {{PHONE}}.

Scope: Work is with adults on anxiety, trauma, relationship patterns, life transitions, and professional burnout. Licensing: {{THERAPIST_NAME}}, {{LICENSE}}.
Confidentiality & privacy: Client information is kept securely. For details ask for the privacy notice or see the intake packet.
